correctness.rationale: For arbitrary n>=3, real a and nonzero b, two independent unit inputs, and integer T>=1, real Fourier eigenbasis blocks factor the exact finite-horizon Krylov Gramian. All normalizations and singular cases are accounted for by two scalar rows, interior 2x2 blocks and classical nonzero-sine products. Moment-Gram determinants are positive precisely at the stated Vandermonde horizons. For even n the exact determinant difference is (det G_E)^2 times a squared residual inner product and is nonnegative, proving the global class comparison. The all-order proof covers eigenvalue degeneracy across k and n-k by real block construction. The standalone dependency-free exact-integer checker separately executed 440 full Gramian determinant tests and 36 even-order comparisons; these finite tests do not prove the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is an exact finite-horizon determinant and two-input cycle D-optimality parity law, not the already-known cycle controllability test or a generic spectral representation. A complete relevant arXiv primary paper, a complete 2011 cycle-leader rank paper, and a complete 2016 reachable-volume paper were inspected for their objects and results. The primary 2011 and 2017 rank analyses do not supply exact Gramian volume formulas; the 2016 projected continuous-time disagreement Gramian is a different objective and cannot imply full-state discrete equalities merely by matching graph/actuator count. No directly established equivalent or dominating result was identified, but an inaccessible later article and unindexed equivalent derivations remain specific risks.
residual_risks: Full text of Liu and Ji (2017) was unavailable during comparison; it is close on two-leader cycle controllability.
Other published treatments of finite-horizon reachability Gramian determinants or circulant systems may contain an equivalent Fourier-factorization corollary not indexed by the searches.
Generic rank, eigenbasis and moment-Gram tools are pre-existing; priority is claimed only for their exact combined all-horizon optimization statement, and is not independently verified.

value.rationale: Exact optimal design of two input locations for an unweighted ring is a motivated finite-horizon reachability-volume problem. The theorem removes any need for a per-distance determinant computation: all relatively prime separations tie for odd order, while for even order the eligible odd class uniformly dominates the even class, for every horizon and every affine Laplacian step. The equality of geometrically different actuator pairs and the nontrivial parity comparison add structural content beyond rank criteria or textbook Gramian definitions. It makes no unsupported claim about unequal gains, other graphs, control-energy norms, or independent scientific certification.
